Aaziko ATES Jarvis — n8n Workflows

How the sales-automation is built in n8n · 5 live workflows · prepared 2026-10-03

The big picture

Jarvis is a sales assistant that helps us find overseas buyers, write grounded emails to them, and never send anything by mistake. It runs on real global-trade data and an AI model (DeepInfra), with a human approving every message.

The 5 n8n workflows below are the plumbing: they receive triggers, look up data, call the AI to draft, run a safety QA, and handle the actual (gated) sending.

One honest note: the AI "brain" for writing outreach & reply drafts was recently moved from n8n into our Node service (for speed, control and a new plan→draft→self-review step). So workflows #1 and #2 show the pipeline design (and still run), while the live drafting now happens in the service. n8n today is primarily the scheduler (#3), the demo mail-loop (#4) and the gated send (#5). The logical flow is identical either way.

Everything runs in SHADOW mode: no email ever reaches a real buyer — only approved test addresses, enforced by workflow #5.

1

Outreach pipeline

n8n workflow · id 8bZxrkES2P3Nt9FG · ● ON
Proactive first-touch — reach a new overseas buyer we found in customs data

What it doesTakes one overseas buyer (for a specific product / HS code) that we discovered in global shipment data, gathers everything we know about them and the product, and writes a warm, honest first-touch email. The draft goes into a review queue — nothing is sent from here.

Real example (human flow)Say we want to approach DEPORSUR SA (Argentina), who regularly imports synthetic-fibre dresses. The salesperson searches the product → picks this buyer. The pipeline automatically looks up: which Indian suppliers make this product, the import duty into Argentina, whether they are already our customer, and the clean product name. It assembles all this as grounded context and asks the AI to write the email — e.g. "We noticed your company imports synthetic-fibre dresses; India is a cost-competitive source; we connect you with vetted suppliers and manage the full export…". An independent QA step then checks the email has invented no fake prices or claims. The approved-looking draft is saved for a human to review. No email leaves the system at this stage.

Node flowBuyer selected (webhook) → Prep → already-contacted check → gate → [Indian-supplier · import-tariff · existing-customer · product-name lookups] → Assemble context → AI writes draft → QA checks it → save to review queue

2

Reply pipeline

n8n workflow · id Lwe3dU9u1aDwLj17 · ● ON
A buyer replied — draft a grounded, honest response

What it doesWhen a buyer replies to our email, this reads their message, pulls up everything we know about them, and drafts a reply — again into the review queue, never auto-sent. It will not invent a price; it asks for the details it needs instead.

Real example (human flow)A buyer emails back: "What is your price for 5,000 pcs?". The pipeline finds their CRM contact, confirms they have not opted out, and pulls their buying-pattern history, the duty, and the product name. The AI deliberately does not quote a number — instead it drafts: "Thanks for your interest — to quote accurately, please confirm the grade and quantity; we will then send a full landed-cost offer with payment terms." QA verifies no fake numbers slipped in, and the draft is saved for human approval. If the sender is not a known buyer (e.g. a logistics or accounts email), it is routed to "triage" and no draft is made.

Node flowBuyer reply arrives (webhook) → Prep → dedup → gate → [contact · suppression/opt-out · buyer-intel · tariff · product-name] → Assemble + decide → AI writes reply → QA → save to review queue (or triage if not a buyer)

3

Auto-ingest scheduler

n8n workflow · id jg4OsLGiZD4uWQMy · ● ON
The automation clock — so nobody has to watch the inbox

What it doesEvery 10 minutes it checks for new buyer replies that have not been processed yet and feeds them to the Reply pipeline automatically. This turns the system from "click each one" into "drafts are ready waiting."

Real example (human flow)At 10:00 a buyer replies to us. By 10:10 the scheduler has picked it up and the Reply pipeline has already prepared a draft response sitting in the review queue. The team simply reviews ready-made drafts instead of monitoring the inbox all day.

Node flowEvery 10 min (timer) → find recent unprocessed replies → build payloads → call the Reply pipeline

4

DEMO mail loop (Gmail)

n8n workflow · id 3Q0zL2wU35z1KUuo · ● ON
Live proof: email arrives → AI reads it → AI drafts a reply, end-to-end on a real mailbox

What it doesConnected to a test Gmail. The moment a mail arrives, it auto-detects it, the AI drafts a proper reply, QA checks it, and the draft is emailed back to ourselves (safe) and saved. This proves that with a real company mailbox the whole loop becomes fully automatic.

Real example (human flow)We send a test email to the demo Gmail, pretending to be a buyer asking about paracetamol API. Within seconds the workflow detects it, the AI drafts a complete reply, QA checks it, and the draft lands back in our own inbox and the review queue — demonstrating the exact flow that a real sales mailbox would run. (It also skips its own drafts, so it never replies to itself in a loop.)

Node flowNew email detected (IMAP) → Prep → skip-our-own-draft? → Assemble → AI writes draft → QA → send the draft to ourselves (SMTP) + save to review queue

5

Approve & Send — GATED

n8n workflow · id 3HLbsO0pEJGNQu43 · ● ON
The safety gate — only approved recipients can ever receive a real email

What it doesThe only place a real email can be sent. A human approves a draft in the panel → it comes here → an allowlist guard checks the recipient. Only approved test addresses pass through to actual sending; every other address is BLOCKED. This guarantees no real buyer is emailed by accident during testing.

Real example (human flow)A reviewer approves a draft addressed to our test address → the Allowlist Guard sees it is on the approved list → the email is sent. If a draft were addressed to a real buyer (say buyer@realcompany.com) → the guard sees it is not on the list → the send is BLOCKED and the system responds "blocked"; nothing goes out. Switching on real buyers is a deliberate, senior-approved change — not something that can happen by mistake.

Node flowApproved draft arrives (webhook) → Allowlist Guard → allowed? → YES: send email (SMTP) · NO: respond "blocked" (no send)

Aaziko Global LLP — internal technical walkthrough. All drafts are human-reviewed; real sending is allowlist-gated (workflow #5). Data sources are read-only; the system only writes to its own review database.
